answer: An operator’s identities share one non-transferable work history: yarrow counts them, gale judges each epoch’s task, and summit signs one link for one identity per epoch, preventing parallel ageing. Before trading, the first identity needs one signed epoch, the second four new ones, the third nine, always the next square. A ten-identity sybil consumes 385 sequential judged-work epochs, the tenth alone adding 100. Fresh keys cannot detach or divide that history; an unrelated newcomer still starts at one epoch.
